Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There may be a brief pause while we poll for questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Industrial Dynamics Corp.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Global Industrial Dynamics Corp.'s performance for the Q3. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. First, our total order intake hit a robust $1.35 billion, up 20% year-over-year, reflecting strong demand across automation, heavy machinery, and electrification segments. Second, we've dramatically improved lead times on key products like our MX-series CNC machining centers and robotic welding cells, now averaging 16.2 weeks company-wide, a 28% reduction from last year. Third, supply chain constraints are easing, with on-time delivery rates for critical components climbing to 87%, thanks to diversification and vertical integration efforts. Fourth, we're advancing our progressive dividend policy, with an annualized payout of $2.80 per share yielding 2.8%, fully covered by free cash flow. And fifth, our share repurchase program has executed $428 million year-to-date, buying back 5.2% of shares at attractive valuations.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, John. Turning to our financial performance, Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. reported $1.25 billion in revenue for the quarter, representing a 16% increase year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 28.2%, driven by pricing discipline, mix shift toward high-margin automation products, and supply chain efficiencies. Operating expenses were $285 million, resulting in an operating income of $268 million. Our net income for the quarter was $185 million, or $1.87 per diluted share.

We are reaffirming our guidance for the full year, with expected revenue growth of 15% and EPS of $6.75 to $7.25. We are committed to returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Good afternoon, everyone. As your CFO, I'm pleased to dive deeper into some of these key metrics starting with our order intake performance, which continues to be a strong leading indicator of our revenue trajectory in the manufacturing and industrial equipment sector. For the quarter, total order intake reached $1.35 billion, marking a robust 20% year-over-year increase from $1.125 billion in Q3 2023. This exceeded our internal guidance and outpaced the industry average of around 10%, as reported in the latest SEMI and Gardner Intelligence indices for capital equipment bookings.

Breaking this down by key segments, our core automation and robotics division, including our flagship IntelliArm collaborative robots and AI-integrated CNC machining centers, drove the majority with $720 million in orders—a stellar 30% YoY surge. This reflects accelerating adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies amid labor shortages and smart factory pushes. Our traditional heavy machinery segment, with hydraulic presses and precision forging equipment supplied to OEMs like Caterpillar and Deere, posted $455 million, up 10% YoY. Emerging electrification products, such as high-voltage battery assembly lines and e-drive test rigs, contributed $175 million, surging 48% YoY as EV supply chains ramp up.

Regionally, North America accounted for 44% at $594 million, up 24% YoY, fueled by reshoring under the CHIPS Act and Inflation Reduction Act, with strength from Tesla and GM gigafactories via modular automation skids and multi-year agreements. EMEA hit $425 million, a 17% increase, bolstered by EU Green Deal mandates for energy-efficient equipment like our low-emission die-casting systems compliant with REACH. APAC, at 35% or $472 million, grew 15% YoY despite softer semiconductor capex, offset by China's NEV boom with orders from BYD and CATL for gigapress tooling.

Our book-to-bill ratio expanded to 1.28x, up from 1.15x last year, with backlog at $4.5 billion providing visibility through FY2025. This is supported by $150 million in R&D for digital twin platforms and edge AI, shortening lead times by 20% and boosting win rates against Fanuc and Siemens. We've tied 65% of new orders to ESG-compliant products, ahead of regulations like U.S. SEC climate disclosures. We're guiding Q4 order intake growth at 16-19% YoY, with upside from QuantumForge hybrid machines gaining aerospace traction for titanium components.

Moving now to our supply chain performance, I'd like to provide a detailed update on lead times for our key products and components—a critical metric for customers where unplanned downtime can cost $50,000 per hour on automotive lines. We've focused on compressing timelines amid semiconductor shortages, volatile steel pricing, and Red Sea disruptions.

Company-wide average lead time for core backlog products—our MX-series CNC machining centers, hydraulic forging presses, and modular robotic welding cells—stood at 16.2 weeks at quarter-end, a 28% YoY improvement from 22.5 weeks and 12% sequential from Q2's 18.4 weeks. High-volume components like proprietary servo motors, PLC controllers, and precision ball screws tightened to 8.7 weeks, down 35% YoY from 13.4 weeks, at the lower end of benchmarks—peers like Haas at 20+ weeks on mills, Fanuc at 18-22 in APAC.

By product line: MX-Series (42% of bookings), 5-axis models at 18 weeks from 26 YoY, via 25% ramp in Ohio foundry capacity, reducing China gray iron reliance amid tariffs. Hydraulic forging presses at 14 weeks from 20, with 10-week alloy steel buffer against 15% inflation per S&P. Robotic welding cells at 12 weeks from 19, via NVIDIA edge AI partnership cutting validation 40%.

Components: Siemens PLCs and rare-earth-free motors at 6 weeks, down 45%, via TSMC dual-sourcing and Guadalajara assembly. Ball screws at 9 weeks, 30% better, with NSK vertical integration bypassing Japan shortages.

Regionally: North America (65% revenue) at 14.8 weeks, nearshoring tailwinds for Ford/GM EV equipment, gaining 2 points share. EMEA (22%) at 17.5 weeks, offset Ukraine steel via Duesseldorf hub at 92% fill rates. APAC (13%) at 19.2 weeks, stabilized by Yaskawa JV ahead of ABB in semis.

Initiatives: Digital Supply Chain Twin with Siemens Xcelerator for 85% visibility, 22% less forecast error, 4.8x turns. AI Demand Sensing with Palantir/SAP cuts reorder 30% via IoT. Resilient ecosystem: 14 sources per component, $150M capex in India/Poland friendshoring.

Shorter lead times are our moat with ISM PMI at 49, IRA $370B subsidies; Tesla/Siemens prioritize sub-20 weeks, in 70% Q3 SLAs. Expect 14 weeks by year-end, supporting $2.8B FY revenue, 18% EBITDA.

Before the financials deepen further, a detailed update on supply chain constraints and component availability, critical for execution and margins. Peers like Caterpillar, Cummins, Deere face similar issues.

Headline: On-time delivery for power electronics, hydraulic valves, forgings at 87% from Q2's 72%, supporting 12% unit shipments, converting $1.2B backlog to revenue.

Semiconductors (15% BOM for IoT CNC/autonomous handlers): MCUs/SiC at 82% fill from 65%, via TSMC/Infineon; inverter lead times 28 weeks, 22% spot premiums hitting margins 150bps. Locked 70% 2024 needs in 18-month contracts.

Metals: HRC down 18% YTD; specialized forgings up 14% YoY from Ukraine energy surcharges. Castings 91%, dual Nucor/Baosteel, inventory $450M (3.5 months).

Hydraulics: 94% from Bosch/Parker, normalized.

Regions: APAC de-risked 40% China rare earths, Taiwan stable. Europe steel +10-12%, reshoring aids backlog €650M wind OEMs. North America Ohio forging Q1'25 cuts leads 40%, Mexico 95% aluminum.

ChainForge $120M YTD: ML/SAP IBP cuts volatility 35%, $25M saved; 12 Tier-1 reservations; SC PCB 50% self-sufficiency FY25; concentration 18% max, 65% multi-sourced.

Inflation contained 8.2% vs industry 11-13%, +220bps EBITDA. Q4 90%+ fill, 15% lead contraction; Red Sea mitigated by air. Underpins FY revenue $4.75-4.85B up 14%, EBITDA 22.5%.

On our dividend policy and yield, a cornerstone of capital allocation in this cyclical sector. We've maintained progressive policy 18 years, 40-50% adjusted EPS payout, balancing returns with growth like next-gen CNC and electrified handling.

TTM adjusted EPS $6.25 supports $2.80 annualized dividend, up 8% from $2.60, 12th increase compounding 7.5% vs S&P Industrials 5.2%. At $98.50 close, 2.8% yield tops Caterpillar 1.6%, Deere 1.4%, Ingersoll 0.9%, via 42% stable aftermarket.

Pillars: FCF coverage 32% payout; Q3 $1.2B FCF up 15%, DIO 78 days via SAP/VMI despite 20% alloy rise.

Industry: PMI >50 seven months, CHIPS fab builds ($450M orders TSMC/Intel); $800M FY24 capex incl. $250M Greenville AI gears >15% IRR.

Regions: NA 55% EBITDA, IIJA backlog $4.1B +22% QoQ; Europe 25% wind down 10% but 65% Dortmund local; APAC 20% +30% CATL/Panasonic batteries.

Guidance: FY25 7-9% growth to $3.00-3.05, 3.0-3.1% yield at $6.75-7.25 EPS. Downside flat via A- rating/$2.5B facility; upside 10%. Board stress-tests GFC-style; attracts 28% income investors, aids ROIC 10-12% amid consolidation like German press tuck-in.

Finally, on our share repurchase program, a cornerstone amid reshoring, Industry 4.0, electrification. $1.2B authorization Feb 2024 post $800M completion.

YTD: 4.8M shares (5.2%), $428M; Q3 $165M at $89.15 avg, 8% below $97.20, 15% below YE'23 $104.50; 11.2x fwd EBITDA vs hist 14.5x, peers 13-15x.

Accelerated: Q1 $112M, Q2 $151M, Q3 opportunistic on election/supply dips; 10b5-1 + blocks.

Accretion: Q3 EPS +12c; YTD +9% adj EPS offsetting EMEA destock. $772M left, Q4 $250-300M.

FCF $512M YTD 115% adj NI, 28% margins from pricing/electrics post-Ukraine. $420M capex funds reshoring.

Regions: NA 58% rev, $3.2B backlog +14% CHIPS/IIJA; APAC 22% moderated China but India CNC +22%; EMEA 20% wind buffer, prioritize buybacks over div.

Technical: VWAP/relative S&P; ESG post-report 25% Scope 3 cuts.

Fortress BS net debt/EBITDA 1.2x, $1.1B liquidity; ROIC >15% WACC. Undervalued vs 8-10% CAGR to 2027; opportunistic to 2025, potential refresh if FCF $700M+.

Now, I will hand over to Lisa Patel, COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Patel (COO):
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've been focused on streamlining our supply chain and improving manufacturing efficiency. Building on the lead time and component wins Michael detailed, we've implemented digital twins, AI forecasting, and supplier diversification, yielding higher throughput and fill rates. We're closely monitoring global disruptions like Red Sea routes and steel volatility, taking proactive steps like Ohio and Guadalajara expansions. We're also investing in automation and digital technologies—NVIDIA AI, Palantir sensing, SAP integrations—to enhance capabilities, supporting book-to-bill strength and ESG orders.

Q&A Session:

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of rising raw material costs on your profitability?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Ben. As I covered in the supply chain update, we've contained inflation to 8.2% YoY versus industry 11-13%, preserving 220 basis points of EBITDA. Steel and aluminum moderated 18% YTD, but forgings rose 14% from energy surcharges—we built buffers and dual-sourced with Nucor/Baosteel. Spot semi premiums added 150bps headwind, but contracts stabilize this. FCF strength and pricing on automation/electrification offset, expanding margins to 28.2%. We're positioned for Q4 gains as fill rates hit 90%+.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez (Goldman Sachs):
What is your outlook for demand in the aftermarket services business?

John Reynolds:
Thanks, Emily. Aftermarket, at 42% of sales, remains resilient, buffering OEM cycles. With backlog visibility and shorter leads drawing more installs, service attach rates are rising—predictive maintenance via digital twins and IoT telemetry boosting uptake 15% YoY. Reshoring and IRA/CHIPS fab builds pull demand for parts in EV battery lines and semi tools. We see mid-teens growth through FY25, supporting dividend coverage and yields above peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
Can you provide an update on your progress in reducing lead times?

Lisa Patel:
Absolutely, David. Echoing Michael's details, we're at 16.2 weeks average, 28% YoY better across MX CNCs at 18 weeks, presses 14, robots 12. Components like motors/PLCs at 6-9 weeks. Regional progress: NA 14.8 via nearshoring, EMEA 17.5 with hubs, APAC 19.2 stabilizing. Digital twin visibility, AI sensing, 14-supplier diversity, and capex in friendshoring drive this—embedded in 70% SLAs. On track for 14 weeks year-end, fueling order conversion.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Closing Remarks:

John Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
